core_obligations: The quadruple (f, d, L, psi) is an element of F_d(T); its morphism r lands in U_d.
It suffices to check the universal-family statement over affine opens: base change makes the functors commute and the twists glue from affine data.
Over an affine base the quadruple and triple functors agree, and the strict functor lemma identifies the universal triple; running the identifications backwards gives theta.
proof_roadmap: Recognize the quadruple as an F_d-point, restrict the universal-family verification to affine opens using base change, and run the triple-to-quadruple translation.
difficulty_reason: Universal-family argument via base change of the functors and the affine triple-quadruple identification; fully displayed with named lemmas.
